abilities.name: Culture
abilities.desc: Measures the nation's interest in and dedication to the arts and sciences, religion and reason, and the pursuit of knowledge.

abilities.name: Economy
abilities.desc: Measures the practical, day-to-day workings of society: production, construction, buying and selling.

abilities.name: Loyalty
abilities.desc: Measures the collective will, spirit, and sense of camaraderie of the citizens.

abilities.name: Stability
abilities.desc: Measures the physical health and well-being of the nation: infrastructure, buildings, and protection.

ruins.name: Corruption
ruins.desc: Citizens sliding into decadence, forbidden knowledge, unethical research, destruction of heritage.

ruins.name: Crime
ruins.desc: Theft, smuggling and rackets that choke prosperity.

ruins.name: Decay
ruins.desc: Physical damage, neglect or degradation of the kingdom, its people and its infrastructure.

ruins.name: Strife
ruins.desc: Treachery, subterfuge, bribery, violence, abuse of power and infighting.

skills.name: Agriculture
skills.desc: Measures the kingdom's ability to work the land, raising crops, herds and livestock.

skills.name: Arts
skills.desc: Measures the kingdom's dedication to entertainment, works of art and public works such as monuments.

skills.name: Trade
skills.desc: Measures the kingdom's involvement in commerce of every kind and the health of its marketplace. You take a cumulative –1 item penalty to Trade checks for every settlement without a Land Border, unless it has at least one Water Border with a Bridge.

skills.name: Defense
skills.desc: Measures the kingdom's ability to watch over and protect itself and its citizens from bandits, monsters, criminals and invasion.

skills.name: Exploration
skills.desc: Measures the kingdom's ability to look beyond its borders and to examine the territory it has claimed up close.

skills.name: Folklore
skills.desc: Measures the kingdom's ties to faiths and customs of every kind.

skills.name: Statecraft
skills.desc: Measures the kingdom's ability to engage and interact with other nations, independent settlements and powers.

skills.name: Warfare
skills.desc: Reflects the kingdom's readiness to mobilise its military forces against its enemies.

skills.name: Industry
skills.desc: Measures the kingdom's dedication to building and manufacturing goods, from basic necessities to luxuries.

skills.name: Engineering
skills.desc: Measures the kingdom's ability to alter the physical landscape of its territory.

skills.name: Intrigue
skills.desc: Measures the kingdom's control over the hidden forces of politics, espionage and criminal investigation.

skills.name: Magic
skills.desc: Measures the kingdom's affinity for the mystic arts, be they arcane, divine, occult or primal.

skills.name: Boating
skills.desc: Reflects the kingdom's affinity for navigating rivers and lakes.

skills.name: Politics
skills.desc: Measures the kingdom's engagement in civic life of every kind.

skills.name: Scholarship
skills.desc: Measures the kingdom's interest in teaching and educating its citizens.

skills.name: Wilderness
skills.desc: Measures the kingdom's ability to manage natural resources, the ecosystem and natural disasters.

charters.name: Conquest
charters.desc: Your sponsor has conquered a territory and its former rulers have been defeated. The people are devoted to your rule (partly out of fear), but the constant threat of war hampers the arts.

charters.name: Expansion
charters.desc: You are entrusted with a domain adjacent to already settled lands. Your sponsor's support helps society, but the dependence leaves the kingdom insecure.

charters.name: Exploration
charters.desc: Your sponsor wants you to explore, clear and stabilise a wild area along the frontier. They guarantee the initial structures, at the cost of a financial debt.

charters.name: Grant
charters.desc: A large sum of unrestricted funds, but you must employ many of your sponsor's citizens and allies, whose loyalties are divided.

charters.name: Open
charters.desc: A true free agent and pioneer: a single boost to any ability and no innate flaw.

heartlands.name: Hill or Plain
heartlands.desc: Your nation starts in an area that is easy to cross; the citizens appreciate that life is easier.

heartlands.name: Forest or Swamp
heartlands.desc: Woods or marshes: no shortage of natural resources or wonders to feed the citizens' imagination.

heartlands.name: Lake or River
heartlands.desc: On the shores of a lake or a river: a built-in engine for trade.

heartlands.name: Mountain or Ruin
heartlands.desc: Mountains or a major ruined site, used to strengthen the defences. Hardy and resilient citizens.

governments.name: Despotism
governments.desc: The government centres on a single individual whose authority is absolute.

governments.name: Feudalism
governments.desc: The government rests on a dynastic royal family, with much of the power spread among vassals and fiefs.

governments.name: Oligarchy
governments.desc: The government is decided by a council of influential leaders who make decisions for everyone else.

governments.name: Republic
governments.desc: The nation draws its leadership from its own citizens, gathered in parliamentary bodies.

governments.name: Thaumocracy
governments.desc: The nation is ruled by the most skilled in magic, who use their knowledge to decide the best ways to govern.

governments.name: Yeomanry
governments.desc: The nation is decentralised and relies on local leaders and citizens to handle the business of government.

roles.name: Ruler
roles.desc: Performs the most important ceremonies, is the chief diplomatic officer, signs all laws and appoints characters to the other high offices.
roles.absence_penalty: −1 to all checks (cumulative with any other vacancy penalty); gain 1d4 Unrest at the start of the Kingdom turn; the Control DC increases by 2

roles.name: Counselor
roles.desc: The link between the government and the citizens: interprets the wishes of the citizenry and advises the other leaders.

roles.name: Emissary
roles.desc: Keeps the secrets of state, oversees clandestine intrigues and manages foreign policy.

roles.name: General
roles.desc: Leads the kingdom's military, directs the armies and commands them in times of war.

roles.name: Warden
roles.desc: Oversees the safety, protection and general health of the kingdom, its lands and its borders.

roles.name: Magister
roles.desc: Responsible for everything magical in the kingdom and for how the supernatural affects the citizens.

roles.name: Treasurer
roles.desc: Oversees the kingdom's funds, the state of business and industry, and matters of taxation.

roles.name: Viceroy
roles.desc: Plans and carries out the expansion and development of the kingdom, in its territories and settlements.

commodities.name: Food
commodities.desc: Spent to Pay Consumption during the Upkeep phase, on famines and disasters, and to keep armies fed in wartime. Gathered with Go Fishing, Harvest Crops or Gather Livestock.

commodities.name: Lumber
commodities.desc: Used to build structures. Harvested from the lumber camps built with Establish Work Site.

commodities.name: Luxuries
commodities.desc: Used to build specialised structures or spent during certain encounters. Found while adventuring, made with Craft Luxuries or gained from events.

commodities.name: Ore
commodities.desc: Used to build structures. Mined from the mines built with Establish Work Site.

commodities.name: Stone
commodities.desc: Used to build structures. Quarried from the quarries built with Establish Work Site.

disconnected_terrain_cost._note: Building on Rugged Terrain: use the highest RP cost among the terrain features of the hex.

hex_features.name: Settlement
hex_features.desc: A village, town, city or metropolis.

hex_features.name: Freehold
hex_features.desc: A settlement that is not part of your kingdom. Bringing it into the kingdom requires a successful Pledge of Fealty. The kingdom gains no XP for improvements already built.

hex_features.name: Bridge
hex_features.desc: An easy overland route across a river: ignore the usual increase in RP cost for Build Roads in that hex. A settlement built here can start with a Bridge structure on a water border.

hex_features.name: Landmark
hex_features.desc: When you add it to the kingdom reduce Unrest by 1d4 and, until the end of the next Kingdom turn, all Culture and Economy checks gain a +2 circumstance bonus. The first Landmark claimed is worth 40 XP.

hex_features.name: Refuge
hex_features.desc: When you claim it reduce one Ruin by 1 and, until the end of the next Kingdom turn, all Loyalty and Stability checks gain a +2 circumstance bonus. The first Refuge claimed is worth 40 XP.

hex_features.name: Resource
hex_features.desc: A particularly dense or lucrative source of Lumber, Ore or Stone: an appropriate Work Site built here doubles the Commodities produced.

hex_features.name: Ruins
hex_features.desc: A partially destroyed structure. Once claimed and cleared you can use its remains as the basis of an appropriate settlement structure, halving its cost.

hex_features.name: Work Site
hex_features.desc: Produces 1 Commodity (Lumber, Stone or Ore) every Kingdom turn, or 2 if it sits in a Resource hex of the matching kind. Commodities are gathered during the Upkeep phase.

hex_features.name: Structure
hex_features.desc: If you clear a hex that contains a Structure, you can add it automatically and for free to a settlement founded there.

hex_features.name: Farmland
hex_features.desc: Every Farmland hex reduces the kingdom's Consumption by 1, as long as it lies within the influence of one of its settlements. You cannot build settlements on Farmland.

hex_features.name: Fortification
hex_features.desc: A protected encampment (a fort or a barbican) built with Fortify Hex. It grants a bonus in war and offers travelling PCs a safe place to rest.

hex_features.name: Roads
hex_features.desc: Travel along roads uses a terrain type one step better than the surroundings.

hex_features.name: Trap or Hazard
hex_features.desc: A Game Master placeholder: something here can hurt. It has no effect on the kingdom or on travel, and comes from no rule: it serves to remember where a danger was put, and to reveal it to the party when they walk into it.

hex_features.name: Dungeon
hex_features.desc: A Game Master placeholder: the entrance of a place to explore. It has no effect on the kingdom or on travel, and comes from no rule: it keeps on the map something that would otherwise live only in the notes.

hex_features.name: Event
hex_features.desc: A Game Master placeholder: something that must happen here. It has no effect on the kingdom or on travel, and comes from no rule: it is a reminder tied to a hex instead of to a separate sheet.

_hex_features_note: The Terrain Features with "source": "table" are not in the rules and carry no Pathfinder 2 mechanics: they are placeholders the Game Master uses to keep the map in order. They are kept apart on purpose, so nobody mistakes them for rules of the game.

travel._note: Transcribed from the Hexploration rules, nothing added. The terrains the rules do not assign to a category stay null: the app stops and asks the GM instead of guessing. The GM can still force the category on a single hex.

hex_size.note: 12 miles (about 21.6 km) from corner to corner: roughly a day to cross.

activities_per_day_table.note: A party this slow takes 2 days for every activity.

travel_speed._page: Exploration and Downtime Modes — Table: Travel Speed
travel_speed._note: How much ground is really covered, for whoever wants the figure in kilometres instead of activities. It is not needed to count journeys between hexes — those go by activities per day, which is another table — but it answers the question «how fast are we going», and the rules give it. The distances hold on flat, clear ground: difficult terrain halves them, greater difficult terrain cuts them to a third. If the journey calls for a check — swimming, climbing — the GM may ask for one every hour and read the progress on this same table.

between_the_lines._note: The table stops at 18 metres (60 feet) and skips 13.5 and 16.5. For those Speeds — and for a faster vehicle — the same proportion continues: 0.6 km per hour for every metre of Speed. It is not an extra rule, it is the rule of the table: that factor reproduces all nine written rows exactly, from the first to the last. In the table in feet it reads as «every 10 feet more is one mile per hour more».

forest.note: The rules give it as difficult or greater difficult: the GM chooses.

lake.note: Water: a vehicle or a swim Speed is needed. The rules assign no fixed category. Whoever sails crosses it as open terrain (see water_and_flight); whoever goes on foot does not pass.

river.note: Downstream it is open terrain, upstream difficult or greater difficult depending on currents and weather. As a terrain it applies to a hex wholly taken by the river: a river flowing between two hexes is marked as a border instead (see borders).

ruins.note: The rules assign no category to this terrain: the table chose the harshest, greater difficult terrain. It is not a rule of the book.

borders._note: The rules know Water Borders and Bridges on the Urban Grid of a settlement (see structures.json, the «Bridge» structure: «Bridges can only be built on Water Borders»), not between the hexes of the map. Bringing the same idea onto the map is a choice of the table: the vocabulary is the game's, the travel rule is not. A border that is not marked is land, and costs nothing.

water.name: Water Border
water.note: A watercourse or a body of water between the two hexes. It cannot be passed without a water vehicle.

ford.name: Ford
ford.note: It can be crossed, but costs one more Travel activity.

bridge.name: Bridge
bridge.note: It can be crossed at no extra cost. It is not the same as the «Bridge» Terrain Feature, which sits on a hex and concerns the RP cost of Build Roads.

current._note: Following a watercourse. The rules say it of the River terrain: downstream it is open terrain, upstream difficult or greater difficult depending on currents and weather. Between the two the rules do not choose, and neither does the app: it counts the easier one and says so, as it does for the forest. Which way the water flows on the map the rules cannot know: the GM marks it on the drawing, stretch by stretch.

downstream.name: Downstream
downstream.note: Going down with the current: open terrain.

upstream.name: Upstream
upstream.note: Going up against the current: difficult or greater difficult depending on currents and weather.

still.name: Still water
still.note: Inside a lake there is no current to follow or go up: there is no direction, and the general line applies — whoever sails finds open terrain almost everywhere (see water_and_flight).

unknown_.name: No current
unknown_.note: A stretch without a direction is water without a current to follow or go up: it is travelled both ways the same, and counts as open terrain. It is the case of every line of a lake, and the table's choice for a river whose direction has not been marked yet. The rules say nothing about a still watercourse: they say that whoever travels on water finds open terrain almost everywhere, and that is where the figure comes from.

roads.note: Travelling on a road improves the terrain by one step. It does not apply to Reconnoiter.

reconnaissance.note: It does not include moving: it is the cost of scouting the hex you are in.

forced_march.beyond: Fatigued until you spend a full day resting.

travel.water_and_flight: If you're flying or traveling on water, most hexes are open terrain.

other_activities.name: Map the Area
other_activities.note: Requires a successful Reconnoiter in the same hex and a Survival check; reduces the DCs to cross by 2.

milestone_xp.desc: Expand a Village into your first Town
Expand a Town into your first City
Spend 100 RP during a Kingdom turn
Expand a City into your first Metropolis

steps.name: Step 1: Assign Leadership Roles
steps.desc: Assign or change leaders with the New Leadership activity (repeatable as many times as you want in this step). Then determine the Vacancy penalties: every unassigned role suffers its own penalty.

steps.name: Step 2: Adjust Unrest
steps.desc: Increase Unrest by 1 for every Overcrowded settlement and by 1 if you are at war. If Unrest is 10 or more the kingdom gains 1d10 Ruin points to distribute and attempts a DC 11 flat check: on a failure it loses a hex. At Unrest 20 or more the kingdom falls into anarchy: you can attempt only Quell Unrest and every check is worsened by one degree.

steps.name: Step 3: Resource Collection
steps.desc: Resource Dice = kingdom level + 4 + bonus dice − penalty dice. Roll them to gain the turn's RP. Then collect 1 Commodity from every Work Site (2 if in a Resource hex). Commodities beyond storage are lost.

steps.name: Step 4: Pay Consumption
steps.desc: Consumption = settlement Consumption + army Consumption − influenced Farmland hexes + event modifiers. Spend Food equal to the Consumption; for every point unpaid spend 5 RP or increase Unrest by 1d4.

steps.name: Step 1: Collect Taxes
steps.desc: You can Collect Taxes once per turn. If you do not, you can attempt a DC 11 flat check: on a success reduce Unrest by 1.

steps.name: Step 2: Approve Expenses
steps.desc: You can attempt Improve Lifestyle or Tap Treasury.

steps.name: Step 3: Tap Commodities
steps.desc: If you have Commodities in stock you can attempt Trade Commodities to increase the turn's RP.

steps.name: Step 4: Manage Trade Agreements
steps.desc: If you have Trade Agreements you can use Manage Trade Agreements.

steps.name: Step 1: Leadership Activities
steps.desc: If the capital has a Castle, a Palace or a Town Hall, every PC with a Leadership Role can attempt up to 3 Leadership activities; otherwise up to 2. A leader cannot attempt the same Leadership activity more than once per turn.

steps.name: Step 2: Region Activities
steps.desc: The PC leaders can collectively attempt up to 3 Region activities.

steps.name: Step 3: Civic Activities
steps.desc: The party can attempt one Civic activity for every settlement of the kingdom.

steps.name: Step 4: Army Activities
steps.desc: Only at war: every army maintained by the kingdom can perform a single Army activity.

steps.name: Step 1: Check for Random Event
steps.desc: DC 16 flat check. On a success a random kingdom event occurs. Otherwise the next turn's DC is reduced by 5. Once the event occurs, the DC goes back to 16.

steps.name: Step 2: Event Resolution
steps.desc: Random events are resolved now. The event's DC is the Control DC modified by the event's level modifier.

steps.name: Step 3: Apply Kingdom XP
steps.desc: A random event is worth 30 XP. The first turn the kingdom spends 100 RP earns 80 XP. Unspent RP convert into XP 1 for 1, up to a maximum of 120 XP per turn.

steps.name: Step 4: Increase Kingdom Level
steps.desc: If XP is at least 1,000 and the kingdom is not at its maximum level (= the party's level), increase the level by 1 and subtract 1,000 XP. At most one level per turn.
